title: 📘 UNIT 8: POST 1991 DEVELOPMENTS IN ETHIOPIA
notes: 1991 → fall of the Derg and beginning of a new political era.

title: 8.1 🏛️ The Transitional Government of Ethiopia
notes:
1991 → Derg regime was overthrown by forces organized under the EPRDF.

June 1991 → National Conference held in Addis Ababa established the Transitional Government of Ethiopia (TGE).

Transitional Charter → provided the legal framework from 1991 until the 1995 Constitution.

Major developments:
• New ethnic- and language-based administrative structure.
• Fourteen regions replaced the former provinces.
• Former armed forces were dismantled and soldiers demobilized.

title: 8.1.1 📜 Transitional Charter
notes:
The Transitional Charter provided the political framework for the transition.

Major principles:
• Establishment of a transitional government.
• Recognition of nations, nationalities and peoples.
• Political participation.
• Preparation of a new constitution.
• Reorganization of the administrative system.

📌 The TGE remained in power until the FDRE Constitution was endorsed in 1995.

title: 8.2 ⚖️ Ethiopia after the 1995 Constitution
notes:
August 1995 → FDRE Constitution endorsed and the Transitional Government ended.

FDRE → Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.

Major features:
• Federal state structure.
• Parliamentary system.
• Multi-party political system.
• Recognition of human and democratic rights.
• Recognition of nations, nationalities and peoples.
• Right to self-determination.

title: 8.2.1 🏛️ Formation of the FDRE
notes:
Meles Zenawi → first Prime Minister of the FDRE.

Dr. Negaso Gidada → first elected President.

Initial federal structure → 9 regional states + Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa city administrations.

Federalism → largely organized around language and ethnicity.

EPRDF ideology → Revolutionary Democracy.

Economy → agriculture-based.

title: 8.2.2 🗳️ Political Parties and National Elections
notes:
The 1995 Constitution replaced the Derg's one-party system with a multi-party system.

General elections mentioned in the textbook:
• 1995 → first general election.
• 2000 → second election.
• 2005 → strong opposition participation and major political controversy.
• 2010 → EPRDF again won the majority according to NEBE.
• 2015 → another general election.

📌 The 2005 election was followed by major protests, arrests and political tension.

title: 8.2.3 🧑‍⚖️ Controversial Article 39
notes:
Article 39 → recognizes the right of every nation, nationality and people to self-determination, including the right to secession.

It also recognizes:
• Right to self-government.
• Cultural and political rights.
• Recognition of national identities.

⚠️ Controversy → some scholars and politicians argue that the article may encourage secession and threaten national unity.

title: 8.2.4 🇪🇹 Ethio-Eritrean War
notes:
1998–2000 → Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a major border war.

Major disputed areas → Badme and Zalambessa.

2000 → Algiers Agreement ended active fighting.

UNMEE → United Nations Mission in Ethiopia and Eritrea established a Temporary Security Zone.

2002 → Ethio-Eritrean Boundary Commission issued its final and binding decision; Badme was awarded to Eritrea.

📌 The decision was not immediately implemented, resulting in a prolonged 'no peace, no war' situation.

title: 8.2.5 🗳️ Challenges of Democratization
notes:
Major challenges included:
• Political disagreement.
• Weak opposition parties.
• Electoral disputes.
• Political protests.
• Human and democratic rights concerns.
• Tensions over federalism and self-determination.
• Difficulty developing a strong multi-party democratic system.

📌 Democratization remained an important political challenge after 1991.

title: 8.3 💰 Socio-Economic Issues
notes:
The EPRDF-led government changed Ethiopia from the Derg's command economy toward a market-oriented economy.

Major changes:
• Private-sector participation increased.
• Capital restrictions on private investors were lifted.
• Government intervention was reduced.
• Infrastructure development became a major priority.
• Roads and education received major government investment.

title: 8.3.1 📈 Economic Development
notes:
Major areas of development:
• Road infrastructure.
• Education.
• Health services.
• Agriculture.
• Industry and investment.
• Energy development.

📌 Since the mid-1990s, road infrastructure and education received major shares of government expenditure.

title: 8.3.2 🌊 Nile Waters and GERD
notes:
Ethiopia sought greater use of the Nile waters for development.

1929 and 1959 Nile agreements → Ethiopia was excluded from the allocation arrangements described in the textbook.

2011 → construction of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) began.

GERD aims →
• Generate hydroelectric power.
• Support economic development.
• Increase electricity production.
• Promote national development.

📌 The project became a major national development undertaking funded substantially through Ethiopian public participation.

title: 8.4 🕊️ Ethiopia's Role in Peacekeeping
notes:
Ethiopia has participated in UN peacekeeping since the 1950s.

Peacekeeping missions included:
• Korea.
• Congo.
• Rwanda.
• Burundi.
• Liberia.
• Sudan.
• South Sudan.
• Somalia.

Ethiopia also contributed to African Union peacekeeping efforts in Somalia.

title: 8.4.1 🇱🇷 Liberia and 🇷🇼 Rwanda
notes:
Liberia → Ethiopian personnel participated in UN peacekeeping operations.

Rwanda → Ethiopian forces participated in UN peacekeeping during the country's post-conflict period.

📌 These missions demonstrated Ethiopia's contribution to international peace and humanitarian operations.

title: 8.4.2 🇸🇩 Sudan and 🇸🇸 South Sudan
notes:
Sudan → Ethiopia participated in UN peacekeeping and humanitarian missions.

South Sudan → Ethiopian personnel also participated in UN peacekeeping operations.

📌 Ethiopia's geographic position and military capacity made it an important contributor to peace and security efforts in the region.

title: 8.4.3 🇸🇴 Somalia and Fighting Terrorism
notes:
Ethiopia contributed to peacekeeping and security operations in Somalia.

Major objectives:
• Support peace and stability.
• Prevent Somalia from becoming a safe haven for terrorist groups.
• Support regional security.
• Cooperate with international and African partners.

📌 Ethiopia also contributed to AU operations in Somalia and participated in efforts against Al-Shabaab.
